title: BoJ Summary of Opinions — March 17-18, 2027 MPM
source: EST: boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/ ('Monetary Policy Meetings'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 41,959 bytes) and parsed row-by-row out of its two year tables by this session. Against the header 'Outlook Report (The Bank's View) | Summary of Opinions | MPM Minutes', the 2027 March row parses exactly as ['Mar. 17 (Wed.), 18 (Thurs.)', '-', 'Mar. 29 (Mon.)', 'May 7 (Fri.)'] — i.e. the Summary of Opinions for the March 2027 MPM publishes 2027-03-29, with no Outlook Report attached to that meeting and the full Minutes following 2027-05-07. Filed estimate on two counts, identical to the five BoJ decision entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:) has FED: for the Federal Reserve and no slot for the Bank of Japan, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Release time is not read off this page and is not asserted here
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2027-03-26 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). It is the first BoJ text of any kind to publish after the two March 2027 Japanese CPI releases, and the ONE TRAP IT CARRIES is that this makes it look like a BoJ reading of them, which it is not: a Summary of Opinions summarises views expressed AT the meeting it names, so this document is written on 2027-03-17/18 and contains no reaction to the national February print (japan-cpi-2027-03-19, estimate) or to the Tokyo March flash and FY2026 Tokyo fiscal average (japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2027-03-26, estimate). The first BoJ venue that actually holds both is the 2027-04-27/28 MPM (boj-decision-2027-04-28, estimate), which is also the first post-food-tax-cut Outlook Report. Why it earns a row anyway: 2027-03-29 is the FIRST US SESSION after a four-day gap — the NYSE is shut Good Friday 2027-03-26 (good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26) and the Tokyo flash lands 19:30 EDT on Thursday 2027-03-25, so nothing US-traded can respond to either Japanese release until this Monday, which then carries three stories at once (this release, the FTC v. Amazon trial opening in ftc-v-amazon-antitrust-trial-2027-03-29, and a three-session quarter-end stub week). That is an attribution hazard worth having named on the calendar rather than rediscovered. Impact is LOW: symbols is empty, no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed, and the BoJ channel to this calendar's AI names runs through yen funding and global term premium, both second-order for a US equity book and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers. Precedent for filing a central-bank meeting-account release as its own entry: fomc-minutes-2026-12-30 and ecb-account-2026-10-08, both kind 'macro-print'. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/boj-summary-of-opinions-2027-03-29.md); id, date, status, kind, impact and symbols UNCHANGED. THE 'LOW IMPACT' CALL IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: all 86 Summaries of Opinions the BoJ has published since the format began (2016-01-08 to 2026-08-10) were parsed today off the Bank's own eleven year archives, and the first US session after one moves the S&P 500 a mean absolute 0.620% against a 0.736% all-day baseline (0.84x, median 0.81x, n=80 inside FRED SP500's rolling ten-year window) — QUIETER than an ordinary session. Nikkei 1.147% vs 0.949% (1.21x) but 0.915% (0.96x) once three global shocks that merely landed on SoO dates are trimmed (2016-06-24 Brexit -7.92%, 2016-11-10 post-US-election +6.72%, 2020-03-25 COVID rebound +8.04%). Same-direction as its own decision day: 41/86 = 48% (Nikkei), 42/84 = 50% (USD/JPY) — a coin flip, so the account carries no directional residual. Regime-normalised on the Fed H.10 fixing, BoJ DECISION days run 1.888 vs a 1.050 all-day mean while SoO days run 1.162, i.e. the account keeps ~13% of the decision's excess; and the BoJ event is a YEN event (1.89x) far more than an equity one (Nikkei 1.14x). THREE CORRECTIONS TO THIS NOTE'S OWN FRAMING. (1) The staleness argument the sibling account ledgers use does not apply: SoO lag is a MEDIAN 10 DAYS (range 7-15 excluding the inaugural 21), against the Fed's stated 21 for minutes and the ECB's stated ~28 for accounts — the BoJ's is the FASTEST meeting account of the three majors, and it is a non-event anyway. (2) '2027-03-29 is the FIRST US SESSION' is a day late: the BoJ page states the release time verbatim ('Summary of Opinions It will be released at 8:50 a.m.'), and 08:50 JST Mon 2027-03-29 is 19:50 EDT SUNDAY 2027-03-28 — into the Globex reopen, and 10 minutes before the 09:00 JST Tokyo cash open. (3) This is not the corridor's only BoJ document, nor its richest: the Bank's 2027 table puts the JANUARY MPM's full, attributed Minutes at Mar. 24 (Wed.), five days earlier and about a meeting that carried an Outlook Report — proposed in the same PR as boj-minutes-2027-03-24 (estimate). ALSO MEASURED: Tokyo is OPEN on Good Friday — JPX's own calendar lists exactly one March 2027 closure, Mon 2027-03-22 (Vernal Equinox observed) — so the four-day gap is US-only and the 03-29 Nikkei bar is clean while the S&P bar is not. AND THE MONDAY INTUITION IS INVERTED: Monday is the modal SoO slot (30 of 86) and the Nikkei's most volatile weekday (1.068%), yet SoO Mondays run 0.964% = 0.90x that matched control, the only weekday below it. THE NOTE'S CENTRAL WARNING SURVIVES ITS TEST and is kept: this text is written 2027-03-17/18 and holds no reaction to Japan's Feb national CPI (2027-03-19) or the Tokyo March flash (2027-03-26) despite publishing after both.
